title: Time Management Training and Student Stress

scenes.narration: This study asks a practical question: can a short time management training help undergraduate students feel less stressed and more in control of time?
scenes.layout_description: Center a student between a tangled clock on the left and a calmer clock on the right.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal hand-drawn black ink illustration on cream background: a student at a desk looks from a messy clock with orange scribbles to an orderly clock with a yellow glow; plenty of white space.

scenes.narration: The authors begin from concern about student mental health, citing Bayram and Bilgel's warning that stress, anxiety, and depression are often neglected.
scenes.layout_description: Show a campus building with a worried student in front and a small warning sign.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink sketch on cream background: simple university building, one student holding books under an orange alert circle, with a yellow question mark above; minimalist style.

scenes.narration: They also cite Pierceall and Keim: in 212 community college students, 75 % reported at least moderate stress, 13 % high stress, and 12 % low stress.
scenes.layout_description: Use three simple vertical bars beside a small group of students.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn bar chart in black ink on cream background: three uneven bars highlighted orange and yellow, with tiny student figures beside them; no extra labels beyond key text.

scenes.narration: Cited research links heightened perceived stress with underachievement, dropout, long-standing illnesses, depression, and unhealthy coping strategies reported by some students in surveys.
scenes.layout_description: Arrange several small icons around a central stressed student.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black line art on cream: central student with tense shoulders, surrounded by simple icons of a falling grade paper, exit door, sickbed, cloud, and bottle, accented with orange arrows.

scenes.narration: Among many student demands, the authors emphasize time-related ones: high workload, time pressure, and the challenge of self-organized learning during university studies.
scenes.layout_description: Place a clock, stack of books, and solo study desk in a loose triangle.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal black ink drawing on cream: heavy book stack, alarm clock, and student planning alone at a desk, connected by orange arrows and yellow highlights.

scenes.narration: Time management interventions are recommended in student support, but the authors note that research on their effectiveness, especially for students, remains scarce.
scenes.layout_description: Show a support desk offering a planner, with only a few research pages nearby.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn black ink scene on cream: campus help desk, a planner handed to a student, and a tiny stack of papers circled in orange to show limited evidence.

scenes.narration: Earlier student studies had examined skills or performance, and one recent study found prevention of increasing stress, not a stress decrease after training.
scenes.layout_description: Draw a timeline with small markers for earlier studies and a question at the end.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink timeline on cream: two small study markers labeled by icons, a stress line held flat in yellow, and an orange question mark at the endpoint.

scenes.narration: So this study tested whether training would increase perceived control of time, decrease perceived stress measured as tension, while demands stayed unchanged.
scenes.layout_description: Use three gauges: one rising, one falling, and one staying level.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal black ink illustration: three simple dashboard dials on cream background, orange arrow up for control, yellow arrow down for tension, flat line for demands.

scenes.narration: The design trained one group, then compared variables expected to change with a control variable, demands, expected not to change after training.
scenes.layout_description: Show one student group going through training, then splitting into two comparison panels.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black hand-drawn group of students enters an orange training circle, then arrows point to two panels: changing dials and an unchanged demands box.

scenes.narration: The paper cites Frese et al.'s argument that this design can help rule out testing, Hawthorne, and nonspecific placebo effects in evaluation.
scenes.layout_description: Draw three possible alternative effects being crossed out beside the study design.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal black ink on cream: a clipboard with the one-group design, and three ghost-like labels represented as simple shadow icons crossed out with orange X marks.

scenes.narration: The four-hour training focused on prioritizing, goal setting, strategy development, daily planning, and monitoring as major parts of the time intervention program.
scenes.layout_description: Arrange five training tools around a central clock.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink sketch: central clock on cream background, surrounded by checklist, target, step ladder, calendar page, and check marks, with orange and yellow accents.

scenes.narration: First, students reflected on academic and extracurricular activities, noted them down, and considered which were most important for their study goals personally.
scenes.layout_description: Show a student sorting activity cards into an important pile.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn student at desk on cream background, sorting small cards with book, club, and study icons; orange circle around the chosen important cards.

scenes.narration: Next, they defined concrete, challenging, proximal goals with deadlines, developed steps, set priorities, planned starts, and considered obstacles and possible responses too.
scenes.layout_description: Show a path from a start line to a target with stones and a small barrier.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal black line art: a path of stepping stones leading to a target, an orange flag for deadline, a small obstacle with a yellow detour arrow.

scenes.narration: Later parts addressed daily planning: what to do, when and where, how much time, avoiding distractions, and monitoring completed tasks each day.
scenes.layout_description: Show a day planner with tasks checked off and distractions pushed aside.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink planner page on cream background with simple time blocks and check marks; phone and noise icons pushed away by orange arrows, yellow checks on completed tasks.

scenes.narration: Forty-eight local undergraduates at a medium-sized German university entered; 23 completed all questionnaires and were used for the main analyses in results.
scenes.layout_description: Show a larger group narrowing through a funnel into a smaller group.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn black ink student figures on cream: many figures at left pass through an orange funnel to fewer figures at right, with yellow highlight around the final group.

scenes.narration: Measures were taken directly before training, 2 weeks after, and 4 weeks after; the training occurred in the middle of semester time.
scenes.layout_description: Use a three-point timeline with the training marked near the first point.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal black ink timeline on cream: three dots, a small training room icon at the first dot, orange arrows moving toward 2 weeks and 4 weeks, yellow semester line underneath.

scenes.narration: For the 23 students, mean age was 23.30 years, SD=2.80; about half were female, 52 %, and subjects varied across different fields of study.
scenes.layout_description: Show a small diverse student group with different subject icons above them.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black hand-drawn group of 23 implied by clustered figures on cream, with icons for different study subjects above; orange and yellow circles highlight age and sex text.

scenes.narration: Before training, most reported no or little experience using time management strategies; 7 reported no experience and 7 little experience in Table 2.
scenes.layout_description: Show two small equal stacks of blank planners beside a few marked planners.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal black ink drawing: two stacks of unused planners highlighted orange, one smaller used-planner stack in yellow, with a student shrugging beside them.

scenes.narration: Time management behaviour used 18 items; tension and demands each used five items; perceived control of time used ten items in questionnaires.
scenes.layout_description: Draw four questionnaire sheets with item boxes of different lengths.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn black ink questionnaires on cream background: one long sheet, two short sheets, one medium sheet, with orange check boxes and yellow pencil.

scenes.narration: After training, reported use of taught strategies increased: nearly significant at 2 weeks, and significant at 4 weeks compared with baseline use.
scenes.layout_description: Show a rising line from baseline to two later points, with the last point emphasized.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal black ink line graph on cream: line climbs from first dot to second to third, orange dotted circle around second dot, yellow strong circle around third dot.

scenes.narration: Two weeks after training, the overall time effect was significant, and tension was significantly lower than before training in the analysis.
scenes.layout_description: Show a tension thermometer lower at the second measurement than at baseline.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black line art on cream: two simple thermometers labeled by timing through key text, first higher with orange stress marks, second lower with yellow calm marks.

scenes.narration: At 2 weeks, perceived control of time showed only a tendency in the expected direction, not a significant increase at that point.
scenes.layout_description: Show a control-of-time dial moving slightly upward but not reaching a marked line.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn black ink gauge on cream: needle nudges upward toward an orange target line but stays below it, with a small cautious yellow arrow.

scenes.narration: Four weeks after training, the overall time effect was significant, with significantly lower tension and significantly higher perceived control of time reported.
scenes.layout_description: Show two paired gauges at the four-week mark, one down and one up.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal black ink on cream: at a four-week timeline dot, one stress gauge points down with yellow calm, and one time-control gauge points up with orange arrow.

scenes.narration: Demands, the perceived self-reported control variable, showed no significant changes from before training to 2 weeks or 4 weeks after the training.
scenes.layout_description: Show a flat demands line across all three measurement points.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink line chart on cream background: three dots connected by a nearly flat line, with a steady stack of work icons underneath and orange equal signs.

scenes.narration: The authors report stronger effects for students with no or little prior experience than for students with moderate or some experience beforehand.
scenes.layout_description: Compare two student groups, with a larger arrow for the no-or-little experience group.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn black ink split panel on cream: left student group with empty planners has a large orange upward arrow, right group with marked planners has a smaller yellow arrow.

scenes.narration: In the authors' interpretation, prioritizing, goals, planning, and monitoring may create orientation, initiate goal-directed behaviour, and provide reinforcing information for students' work.
scenes.layout_description: Show a student moving from a messy map to a clear route with check marks.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimal black ink illustration: student follows an orange path on a simplified map from scattered tasks to a target, with yellow check marks appearing along the route.

scenes.narration: The takeaway is cautious: this preliminary, small-sample study suggests benefits, but larger studies and stronger comparison designs are still needed for conclusions.
scenes.layout_description: End with a balanced scale holding the finding on one side and future research on the other.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black hand-drawn scale on cream background: one pan holds a small clock and calm student, the other holds larger research papers, with orange and yellow highlights.
